newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt warns of trade war with U.S. over GMOs.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt warns of trade war with U.S. over GMOs.

text.p: The European Union is risking a damaging trade war with the United States in its aversion to imported produce derived from genetically modified organisms (GMOs) German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said.

In an interview with the business daily Handelsblatt, Rexrodt said if the EU dragged its feet over admitting modified maize and rapeseed imports in the autumn, there could be "grave trade problems" not only with the U.S., but also Canada.

As approval for imports of individual products had now taken more than 20 months, the EU may be forced to keep uncleared material in store on arrival at EU ports even if its GMO content was as low as 0.1 percent.
The EU should approve the applications to avoid arguments and should not cause unnecessary delays if there were no safety risks.
Rexrodt said the U.S. appeared already unhappy with labelling options presented last week by the EU Commission for products containing GMOs.

These are aimed at appeasing sensitive European consumers but the U.S. sees no need to label products if they do not endanger human health and fears this could pave the way for a costly segregation of GMO and conventional farm products.

Rexrodt said some 40 percent of food products on offer had already been touched in some way by technical processes and by contents that were genetically engineered. Labels stating the possibility GMOs may be contained in such products were already telling consumers what they needed to know. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-49103275
